description:
Found during the bedrock-m7j audit; pre-existing.

`SegmentRecycler.Logic.allocate_file/2` (lib/bedrock/data_plane/log/shale/segment_recycler.ex:174-197) opens the file with `:exclusive` — creating it — then calls `:file.allocate/3`. If the allocation fails, the `after` block closes the fd but never removes the file, and `next_id` advances only on success.

So a failed preallocation leaves `preallocated.N` on disk at zero length.

## Failure scenario

The log's filesystem fills. `:file.allocate/3` fails with `:enospc`, leaving an empty `preallocated.N`. The recycler stops. On the next incarnation `Logic.new/4` calls `find_existing_preallocated_files/1` (:121), which globs `preallocated.*` and adopts every match into the pool with no size check — so the recycler starts believing it holds a 64 MiB preallocated segment that is actually 0 bytes.

A checkout then hands that file to `Writer.open/3`, which derives `bytes_remaining` from `stat.size` (writer.ex:41). With size 0 the arithmetic yields a negative remaining budget, and the segment is unusable as a WAL segment while presenting as a healthy one.

Not introduced by bedrock-m7j, but that ticket adds one more trigger for the continue that runs `create_new_segments/2`.

## Fix

Remove the file when `:file.allocate/3` fails — the `after` block already runs, so it is the natural place. Consider also validating size in `find_existing_preallocated_files/1`, so a partially-written pool file from any cause cannot be adopted as whole; that is the same 'absence is the only thing that excludes' reasoning applied to segments.

## Test (write first, must fail)

Force an allocation failure (a tiny filesystem, or an injected `:file.allocate` fault) and assert no `preallocated.*` file remains. Separately, plant a zero-length `preallocated.1` and assert `Logic.new/4` does not adopt it.
title: [BUG] A failed segment preallocation leaves a zero-length file the next incarnation adopts as a full segment
